initial_scene: Robot-mounted forward view with both robot forearms entering from the lower corners. A multicolored Rubik's cube rests on the highest wooden shelf, a person stands behind it, and the lowest wooden tray-like shelf is empty.

observed_sequence.observation: Person touches and turns the cube on the highest shelf, changing the visible front face from blue to yellow; the cube remains on that shelf. Both robot hands start open.
Person withdraws their hand. Right robot arm rises toward the cube; left robot arm remains near its initial open-hand position.
Right hand reaches across the upper shelf and closes its thumb and fingers around opposite sides of the cube; the cube tilts as grasp is established.
Right hand lifts cube visibly clear of the upper wooden surface, initially upward and toward the robot's right.
Right arm transports cube downward to the lowest tray-like wooden shelf and lowers it to the shelf surface.

Cube settles on the bottom shelf. Right fingers begin opening at the end, with the upper fingers rising away from the cube; hand and thumb remain immediately beside the cube as the clip ends. No complete arm withdrawal is shown.

anatomical_side_evidence.right_hand: Active arm enters from the robot's right/lower-right edge; its thumb is on the inner/left side and fingers curl from the outer/right side around the cube, consistent with anatomical right hand.
anatomical_side_evidence.left_hand: Inactive near arm enters from lower left with thumb toward the inner/right side, supporting the forward-view convention.
anatomical_side_evidence.confidence: high; robot torso is out of frame, but arm origins, forward viewpoint and opposing thumb positions establish the convention.

arm_hand_roles.left: Remains open near initial position throughout; no object contact or stabilization.

terminal_state: Cube is on the lowest wooden shelf with green face upward; right fingers are opening beside it, with thumb and palm still nearby. Complete hand withdrawal is outside the clip.
uncertainties: Final cube-to-shelf contact is partly obscured by the right hand; lowering, settled position and finger opening support set-down, but complete clearance of all hand contact is not visible.
